2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under;
The Petitioner and the respondent No.1 are husband and wife and their marriage was solemnized on 29.04.2016 at Crl.Misc.88/2021 VSK Garden, Greater Noida, U.P. and from the wedlock they have one child.

Further she submitted that, at the time of marriage respondents family had given some gold ornaments to the petitioner and her parents also given some gold ornaments to the respondent no.1 and to her.

After marriage she started to live with respondents at matrimonial house and on 09.05.2016 respondent No.2 demanded all jewels given to her and she handed over the all the jewellery and money to respondent No.2.
Further she submitted that, respondent No.2 took away all the gifts and money which the petitioner had received on her wedding.

Further she submitted that,
on 11.05.2016 petitioner and respondent No.1 went to her parents house at Lucknow for the first time after their marriage and at that time respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 were taunting the petitioner constantly on minor things.
Petitioner went back to Delhi to her matrimonial home on 19.05.2016 along with her father.

At that time respondent No.1 had already left for his office and respondent No.2 demanded a bed from her father and respondent No.2 purchased a bed for Rs.71,845/- and a mattress for Rs.45,800/- on 8 th and 10th June 2016 and demanded that the petitioner pay for it.

Further petitioner submitted that, on 24.05.2016 she went to Lucknow with her father in law for her first Vat-Savitri Pooja for that respondent No.1 was also invited and he had promised the petitioner that he would join her but eventually did not turn up for it and later on 06.06.2016 he asked the petitioner to come back to Delhi and demanded to book return tickets by her parents or her brother.
Respondent No.1 slowly began alienating the petitioner and stopped taking responsibility for the petitioner both emotionally and financially.

Respondent No.1 used to taunt Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/
2 and abuse the petitioner frequently and right from around 10 th June 2016 he began threatening the petitioner by telling her that if she didn't accede to his unreasonable demands he would divorce her.
Petitioner was interested in teaching and she got interview call from reputed schools at Greater Noida but Respondent No.2 has not allowed her to go for the interview and told her that teaching is a cheap job.

Further she submitted that, respondent No.1 was not interested in registering the marriage but finally on 15.07.2016 the petitioner and respondent No.1 got registered their marriage during that time respondent No.2 told the respondent No.1 that he should sign the papers carefully since in case the parties get divorced in the future then the petitioner Crl.Misc.88/2021 would not be entitled to any share in the property.
Petitioner was slowly becoming aware that the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 were already thinking of ways to abandon the petitioner for no rhyme or reason.

On 24.07.2016 her parents visited her at matrimonial place for the first time but respondent No.2 was unhappy about their visit and told to her mother that petitioner was cheap and a prostitute because she sat on the sofa beside her husband respondent No.1.
4.
Petitioner has alleged that, she found out she was pregnant on 24.07.2016 and very exited to share good news with her family but respondent No.1 fought with her.

She has further alleged that,
during her pregnancy she was forced to take care of herself with her parent's support since respondent No.1 and their family were detached and abusive.
She has alleged that, she was not allowed to rest during her pregnancy because respondent No.2 believed that baby would be born dumb if she slept in the afternoon.

She has further alleged that, respondents used to pick up quarrels with her during her pregnancy without being bothered about her and unborn child and also threatened the petitioner that he will give divorce.
She has further alleged that, respondent No.2 took all way all her jewelry which she Crl.Misc.88/2021 had kept in the locker.

She has further alleged that, on 03.10.2016 when her parents came to her matrimonial home and requested respondent No.2 to send the petitioner to Lucknow for a few days, respondent No.2 denied their request and respondent No.1 also started abusing petitioner and her family.
They cursed the petitioner and her family.
Since petitioner became terrified for her safety she decided to leave with her parents to Lucknow.
Thereafter, respondents did not visit or care for the petitioner during her pregnancy.
She has further alleged that, after her son was born on 24.03.2017 respondent No.1 did not even listen to the news and disconnected the call and respondent No.2 fought with petitioner's mother.

She has alleged that, the entire medical expenses of the petitioner during delivery and medical expenses of the child came up to Rs.1,15,912/- and the entire vaccination charges amounting up to Rs.50,000/- which are borne by the petitioner's parents.

She has further alleged that, even after she went back to the matrimonial home respondents would unnecessarily taunt her,
abuse her and pick up fights with her.

She has stated that, on 07.08.2017 when her cousin visited her house respondent No.1 picked up a fight with her and threatened her brother and even told her brother that he Crl.Misc.88/2021 had slapped her previous day.

Since petitioner's brother realized it would be unsafe for the petitioner to continue live in the matrimonial home he helped her pack her things and he took her to their aunts place in Dwaraka and from there they left to Lucknow to her parents house.
She has alleged that, she has left her valuables at respondent's house but respondents refused to give them back to her.
She has further alleged that, respondent No.1 never tried to contact the petitioner after the said incident and he has not taken a responsibility of the petitioner and the child.
She has stated that, she has sent email to respondent No.1 asking him why he had abandoned her but there was no response from respondent No.1.

Even effort for reconciliation from petitioner's Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/
3 family have been refused by respondents.

11. In this case, there is no dispute regarding the relationship between parties.

the petitioner and respondents resided together till the date of separation.

Only the aspect of domestic violence needs to be proved by the petitioner.

12. In order to prove that, the respondents have committed domestic violence, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and filed her affidavit in lieu of examination in chief wherein she has reiterated the contents of her petition.
She has produced 26 documents and got them marked as Ex.P.1. to 26.
In support of her petition she has got marked Ex.P.4 to 6, Ex.P.8 to 13 are related to the educational expenses of the child.
Ex.P.2, 3, 7 are the bank statements of the petitioner's account at SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI.

Ex.P.21 to 23 are the rental agreements of the petitioner, Ex.P.24 to 26 are emails sent by the petitioner to respondent No.1 on 13.12.2017, 22.12.2017 and 31.12.2017 respectively, asking the respondent No.1 why he had abandoned her.
Petitioner in her cross examination has admitted that, she has not submitted bills, receipts regarding marriage expenses.
She has stated that, she has produced her bank statement regarding purchase of mattress.
She has stated that, respondent No.1 has not paid any maintenance towards the child before the Court order.
She has stated that, she has not shown the child to the respondent No.1 as he Crl.Misc.88/2021 has not approached her to see the child.

She has stated that, respondent No.1 was taking care of the household expenses but he was not taking care of her expenses and she was managing her expenses through her savings and money given by her father.
She has stated that, respondent No.1 and 2 have been threatening her with divorce since the first month of marriage.
She has stated that, she has resided with respondent No.2 for 6 months.
She has denied the suggestion that, she voluntarily left to her maternal home during her pregnancy.
She has stated that, she has been residing in her parents house since 2017.
Now she has taken a rented house and she is residing there.
She has stated that, she is receiving a salary of Rs.64,000/- per month.
From the cross examination of the petitioner it can be gathered that she has withstood the test of cross examination and nothing has been elicited from her to disbelieve her evidence.
The documents submitted by the petitioner clearly shows that, respondent No.1 has not maintained the petitioner and her child from separation till interim maintenance was awarded by the Court.
It is an admitted fact that, petitioner was not employed at the time of marriage and separation.
Petitioner has completed her MBA after separating from the respondent No.1 and she has secured a job for Crl.Misc.88/2021 herself.
This is not denied by the respondents.
She has stated that, she has taken a loan of Rs.15 lakhs from her father for meeting her educational expenses.
However, there is no evidence before this Court for the same.

The very fact that, respondent No.1 being the father of minor child and husband of petitioner who was not employed at the time of separation has failed to maintain them itself constitutes domestic violence.
Further the emails produced by the petitioner marked as Ex.P.24 to 26 shows that, the petitioner has pleaded with respondent No.1 to talk to her.
But respondent No.1 has not replied or responded to the petitioner.
These emails are not denied by the respondent counsel during the cross examination.
From the date of the emails it can be gathered that they were sent when the child was 9 months old.
The fact that, respondent No.1 did not respond to the emails or take up the responsibility of the petitioner and her child constitutes economic abuse, mental and emotional abuse.
13. Respondent No.1 has examined himself as R.W.1 but he has not appeared for his further examination in chief and his cross examination.
Hence, his cross examination was taken as nil.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vidyadhar V/s Manik Rao reported in Crl.Misc.88/2021 1999 (3) SCC Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/
5 573 has held that "where a party to the suit does not appear into the witness box and state his own case on oath and does not offer himself to be cross examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct as has been held in a series of decisions passed by various High Courts and the Privy Council....."

entities.text: Vidyadhar V/s Manik Rao reported in Crl.Misc.88/2021 1999 (3) SCC Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, if a party abstains from entering the witness box it would give raise to an adverse inference against such party U/Sec.114 of Indian Evidence Act.

By applying this proposition of law to the present case it is seen that the respondent No.1 did not appear before the Court and offer himself to be cross examined in spite of sufficient opportunities.
Hence, an adverse inference has to be drawn against respondent U/Sec.114 of Indian Evidence Act and the Court is compelled to conclude that the case set up by the respondent No.1 is false.
Further respondent No.2 also did not chose to lead her evidence.
Hence, an adverse inference has to be drawn against the respondents that the case set up by them is false.

14. It is an admitted fact that, respondent No.1 is working as Assistant Director General,
Government of India.
He has stated that, his net pay is Rs.1,20,279/-.
Hence, he has the capacity to maintain the petitioner and Crl.Misc.88/2021 her child.

As already discussed the very fact that,
respondent No.1 did not pay anything towards the maintenance of the petitioner and her child till the order of this Court proves that he has committed domestic violence.
As already stated respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court and examined herself.
There is nothing elicited from the petitioner in her cross examination to disbelieve the allegations made by the petitioner against respondent No.2.
Hence, point No.1 answered in the affirmative.
15. Point No.2 :- The petitioner has sought for monthly maintenance of Rs.94,000/- for herself and the child.

She has also sought for one time basic annual expenses for herself and her child amounting to Rs.6,55,000/- and she has sought for Rs.22,05,912/- for expenses incurred for basic maintenance of the petitioner and the child over the past 5 years.
16. The respondent has filed his assets and liability affidavit.

He has stated that, he has studied B.E.
Electronic and Communications and PG Diploma in Metro Rail management.
He has stated that, he is working as Assistant Director General for Government of India and he is getting net pay of Rs.1,20,279/-.
He has Crl.Misc.88/2021 stated that, he is receiving Rs.5,000/- per month as bank interest.
He has stated that, he has incurred marriage expenses of his sister, educational fee for higher studies and medical expenses of his aged parents.
He has stated that, he does not have any properties.
He is not paying any EMI towards loan.

He has stated that, he requires Rs.1,17,415/-
towards monthly expenses.
He has given a break up of the monthly expenses and stated that, he has kept a reserve of Rs.15,000/- per month towards his child's expenses.
He has submitted his bank statement from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2022.
He has submitted bill from travel agency to show that he is incurring traveling expenses from Greater Noida to Delhi of Rs.10,000/- every month.
He has submitted rent receipt to show that he is incurring rent of Rs.35,000/- per month.
He has submitted electricity bill to show that he is incurring Rs.7,631/- towards electricity.
He has submitted maintenance charge and accounts statement issued by the Residents Association of his rented flat wherein the maintenance charges is stated to be Rs.3,797.50 per month.
He has submitted his IT return for assessment year 2021-22 which shows that his total income as Rs.13,13,240/-.
As per the IT return he is getting interest from bank deposit of Rs.1,94,136/-.

He has submitted IT return acknowledgment for the year Crl.Misc.88/2021 2022-23 which shows his total income as Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/
6 Rs.12,33,740/-.

sentences.text:
He has submitted his pay slip shows that his total salary is Rs.1,52,001/- and net pay as Rs.1,20,279/-.
17.

On the other hand the petitioner has filed her assets and liabilities affidavit wherein, she has stated that, she is employed and she is working at Price Water House Coopers as Associate consultant and getting salary of Rs.51,000/- per month.
She has submitted her employment offer letter and pay slip in this regard.
Her pay slip reveals that, her gross salary is Rs.62,075/- and net pay is Rs.51,532/-.
She has also submitted offer letter issued by company called Input Zero and pay slip issued by the said company.
She has stated that, she has joined the said company on 04.08.2020 as Client Engagement Manager and her pay slip for August 2020 shows that she is getting net salary of Rs.50,880/-.
She has stated that, she is residing in a rented house and she is paying Rs.35,000/- towards rent and Rs.1,50,000/- towards security deposit.
She has submitted rent agreement in this regard which are marked as Ex.P.21 to 23.
Ex.P.23 is the rent agreement for the year 2023 wherein the rent is increased to Rs.38,587.5 per month.
She has submitted that, she requires Rs.94,000/- per Crl.Misc.88/2021 month towards monthly expenses.
She has stated that, she requires Rs.1,10,000/- towards school fees and Rs.3,00,000/- towards child care expenses.
In this regard she has submitted her child's school fee receipts marked as Ex.P.4 to 6 and 8 to 13.
She has stated that, she has taken loan of Rs.15 lakhs from her father for her MBA.
She has stated that, she has no properties and she has no liabilities.

18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324 it is held that,
when both spouses are earning sufficiently they have to contribute equally towards the expenses of the child.

entities.text: Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent is duty bound to maintain the child.
However, in this case the respondent No.1 is earning more than the petitioner.

Since petitioner has the custody of the child and she is residing in a rented house she is incurring expenses towards the education, extra curricular activities, day to day expenses, rent, household expenses, flat maintenance, medical expenses of the child and herself from her income.
This is apart from actually taking care of the needs of the child.
The income of the petitioner is very much less compared to that of respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 being the father and the husband has to maintain the petitioner Crl.Misc.88/2021 and the child.
Even though the petitioner is earning respondent No.1 has a duty to provide for shelter and the expenses of the child.
Petitioner has sought for Rs.40,000/- for rent and Rs.1,50,000/- towards security deposit.

Apart from that, she has sought for monthly maintenance of Rs.94,000/- and Rs.22,05,912/- for the expenses incurred by her for the cost 5 years, Rs.6,55,000/- towards one time expenses for the petitioner and her child.
Respondent No.1 has submitted his pay slip for October 2022 which states his net pay Rs.1,20,279/-.
Considering respondent No.1 is a government employee he is bound to have received increments, promotion etc.,
Hence, his salary is bound to have increased.
Respondent No.1 has stated that, he is ready to pay Rs.15,000/- per month towards the child's expenses and he has reserved the amount.
However, respondent No.1 has not accounted for the increase in the educational and living expenses of the child and Rs.15,000/- is grossly insufficient in the current standard of living.
Respondent No.1 has given a break up of his monthly expenses and also submitted certain documents in support of the expenses incurred by him.
It is an admitted fact that, respondent No.2 is dependent on him.

On the other hand petitioner has not given a break up of her expenses especially with respect to Crl.Misc.88/2021 incurring Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/
7 Rs.22,05,912/- for the past 5 years.

entities.text: Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She has also not explained the claim of Rs.6,55,000/- made by her.
Since, the maintenance is awarded from the date of the petition expenses such as medical expenses, travel expenses, expenses incurred for social gathering will be included in the same.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case the Court has to consider the status of the parties, earning capacity of the parties, needs and expenses of the petitioner, number of dependents on the respondent, expenses of the respondent, educational qualification of the parties,
whether the petitioner has independent source and whether the same is sufficient to enable her to maintain herself, standard of living as she was accustomed to in the matrimonial home, whether she was working before marriage, cost of litigation for a non working wife etc., while ordering for maintenance.
Considering all the above factors petitioner's child is s entitled for monthly maintenance of Rs.25,000/- per month for day today expenses like food, clothing, education and shelter.
The respondent No.1 is also directed to pay Rs.10,000/- per month to the petitioner towards rent.

19. The petitioner has sought for direction to the respondents to pay compensation and damages of Crl.Misc.88/2021 Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the physical and mental torture suffered at the hands of the respondents and litigation expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-.

Sec.22 of PWDV Act states, Magistrate may grant compensation in addition to the other reliefs that may be granted under this Act and direct the respondent to pay compensation and damages for injuries including mental torture and emotional distress caused by the acts of domestic violence committed by the respondent.
As discussed in point No.1 it is proved that the respondents have subjected the petitioner to domestic violence and she has incurred litigation expenses as well.
The respondents have not maintained the child after the separation.
The child is growing up without the presence of his father i.e., the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 has not made any attempt to even visit the child till now.
The petitioner after separation has been compelled to restart her life and also look after the child by herself due to the conduct of the respondent No.1.
petitioner has even completed her MBA degree after separation and she has secured a job while she was taking care of a small child.
No amount of money can compensate for the hardship undergone by the petitioner due to the conduct of the respondents.
However, U/Sec.22 of PWDV Act, she is entitled for compensation.
Hence, respondent No.1 is Crl.Misc.88/2021 directed to pay an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees ten lakhs only) to the petitioner towards compensation.

Respondent No.2 is an aged lady and she has no independent source of income hence even though it is proved that she has committed domestic violence since she does not have the financial capacity to pay the compensation no order is passed against her.

Hence,
point No.2 answered partly in the affirmative.

20. POINT No.3 :- In view of the materials placed before this court, pleadings, deposition and documentary evidence this court proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is allowed in part.

The respondents has neglected the petitioner without any reasonable cause and the respondents are capable to provide maintenance to the petitioner.
Hence, it is proved that the petitioner and the respondents are in domestic relationship.
It is also an admitted fact that,
the petitioner and respondents resided together till the date of separation.
Hence they have resided together in a shared household.
Hence,

petitioner and the child were in a domestic relationship with the respondents in Crl.Misc.88/2021 a shared household.
Only the aspect of domestic violence needs to be proved by the petitioner.
However, there is no evidence before this Court for the same.
The very fact that, respondent No.1 being the father of minor child and husband of petitioner who was not employed at the time of separation has failed to maintain them itself constitutes domestic violence.
Further the emails produced by the petitioner marked as Ex.P.24 to 26 shows that, the petitioner has pleaded with respondent No.1 to talk to her.
But respondent No.1 has not replied or responded to the petitioner.
From the date of the emails it can be gathered that they were sent when the child was 9 months old.
The fact that, respondent No.1 did not respond to the emails or take up the responsibility of the petitioner and her child constitutes economic abuse, mental and emotional abuse.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vidyadhar V/s Manik Rao reported in Crl.Misc.88/2021 1999 (3) SCC Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/
5 573 has held that "where a party to the suit does not appear into the witness box and state his own case on oath and does not offer himself to be cross examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct as has been held in a series of decisions passed by various High Courts and the Privy Council....."
Hence, an adverse inference has to be drawn against respondent U/Sec.114 of Indian Evidence Act and the Court is compelled to conclude that the case set up by the respondent No.1 is false.
Further respondent No.2 also did not chose to lead her evidence.
Hence, an adverse inference has to be drawn against the respondents that the case set up by them is false.
Hence, he has the capacity to maintain the petitioner and Crl.Misc.88/2021 her child.
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324 it is held that,
when both spouses are earning sufficiently they have to contribute equally towards the expenses of the child.
The respondents have not maintained the child after the separation.
The child is growing up without the presence of his father i.e., the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 has not made any attempt to even visit the child till now.
The petitioner after separation has been compelled to restart her life and also look after the child by herself due to the conduct of the respondent No.1.
petitioner has even completed her MBA degree after separation and she has secured a job while she was taking care of a small child.
No amount of money can compensate for the hardship undergone by the petitioner due to the conduct of the respondents.
However, U/Sec.22 of PWDV Act, she is entitled for compensation.
Respondent No.2 is an aged lady and she has no independent source of income hence even though it is proved that she has committed domestic violence since she does not have the financial capacity to pay the compensation no order is passed against her.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is allowed in part.
Respondent No.1 is hereby directed to pay an amount of Rs.25,000/- per month (Rupees twenty five thousand only) to the petitioner's child by name Master Pranav towards maintenance from the date of the petition till attaining majority.
